title: Bacterial aggregation in the presence of directed motion
authors: Timothy Power, Hildur Knutsdottir, Leah Edelstein-Keshet, Theodore Kolokolnikov
abstract: We model directed motion of cells that aggregate into a cluster in the presence of chemotaxis or fluid transport. Starting from a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) of Galante \& Levy (2013), Chavy-Waddy \& Kolokolnikov (2016), we consider two model variants, with (I) directed motion of individuals, or (II) implicit individual bias in one direction. In both cases, we derive fourth order nonlinear PDEs representing the continuum limits of the models as a generalization of Chavy-Waddy \& Kolokolnikov (2016). An exact analytic solution then describes cluster density profile as well as the group velocity, and we identify the regimes where the travelling cluster exists. Excellent agreement is observed between the discrete models and the exact solutions of the PDEs in both models, including the existence and speed of the travelling cluster.
summary: This work develops a continuum PDE model to describe how bacterial clusters form and move under directed forces like chemotaxis. By generalizing previous models, the authors provide analytical solutions for the cluster's speed and map out stability regimes, showing excellent agreement between discrete simulations and the derived PDE theory.
main_problem: The paper models the aggregation of bacteria into clusters when subjected to directed motion, such as chemotaxis or fluid transport.
main_result: The authors derived a fourth-order nonlinear PDE that accurately describes the cluster density profile and group velocity, identifying distinct regimes for cluster existence and speed.
method: The continuum limit was derived from stochastic Agent-Based Models (ABMs) using Taylor expansion, leading to a generalized nonlinear PDE solved via a traveling pulse ansatz.
model_or_system: The system models bacterial aggregation using two variants: Model I (intrinsic directed motion $v$) and Model II (implicit directional bias $r$). The dynamics are captured by a fourth-order PDE.
key_observables: Cluster density profile, group velocity (speed of the travelling cluster), and stability regimes (e.g., bistability or 'gap' regions).
important_parameters: Directed motion parameters ($v$ or $r$), aggregation strength ($b$), and diffusion coefficients ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$ in the PDE).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption of a small bin spacing ($h 	o 0$) for the PDE limit, and the analysis uses traveling wave ansatz solutions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition of the cluster state as velocity increases (localized $	o$ homogeneous) and show bifurcation diagrams revealing 'gap' and bistability windows for the two models.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the ABM foundation, deriving the continuum PDE limit, and then analyzing the resulting PDE using traveling wave solutions to determine the cluster speed and stability boundaries for both motion models.
why_interesting: While focused on biology, the mathematical framework—deriving complex nonlinear PDEs from discrete stochastic processes and analyzing traveling wave solutions—is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and pattern formation in complex systems.
